finding.claim: Authentication is taken from a client-supplied HTTP header (X-Session-User-Verified) with no verification of a session, signature, or that a trusted proxy set it. Any caller can impersonate any user named in a resource's grants and pass the ACL checks, which allows deleting or renaming other users' files. The root cause is a single missing authentication control in load_user, so both routes are listed under this one finding.
finding.source: Request header X-Session-User-Verified, set by any unauthenticated remote client
finding.sink: del STORE[fid] in delete_file (views.py:18) and f["name"] = request.json["name"] in rename_file (views.py:27), gated by acl.is_allowed (acl.py:5)

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified") — raw header value becomes the identity, with no validation
delete_file calls ensure_allowed(g.user, f, "delete"), which only checks membership of the attacker-chosen name in resource grants
is_allowed does `action in grants.get(user, [])`, so a spoofed owner name passes
rename_file uses the same g.user for the "write" check, then mutates the file name at line 27

finding.guards_checked: Searched the whole repo, which contains only acl.py and views.py. There is no signature, session lookup, or token check, and no code that strips or overwrites the header at the app layer. The ACL check is enforced correctly in both handlers (the ensure_allowed result aborts, and is_allowed returns 403), but it keys on the spoofable identity. An unauthenticated request with no header gives g.user=None, which only matches a grants entry for None, so spoofing a real user name is what exploits it. Any trusted-proxy stripping of the header would be outside this code, and none is configured or enforced here.

verdict.guard_found: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) and is_allowed (acl.py:5, checked at views.py:25) are enforced correctly, but they key on the spoofable g.user. No signature, session lookup, or proxy-header stripping exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 takes g.user straight from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header, so an anonymous caller who names a grantee passes the ACL at acl.py:5, and both the delete (views.py:18) and the rename (views.py:27) go through.
